findings.description: The scratch dir now sits inside the main repo's git dir. It is deleted only on a dry run that finishes cleanly (line 329). When `plantCommit` throws (for example the `find string must occur exactly once` check at L107-108), or a later step throws before L329, a `.git/review-eval-*` dir with partial `<case-id>.index` files is left behind. Every `--run` also leaves one, holding the index files as well as results.json. Before this change these dirs went to tmpdir, where the OS clears them. Inside .git nothing removes them, not even git gc, so they pile up with no notice.

The README says `results.json` sits in a `review-eval-*` folder of the git directory, but it doesn't say the folder is kept after `--run`. Only the dry run removes it (line 329), and nothing in the `--run` path does. The README also says `results.json` is rewritten after each case, so a reader who wants the scores has to find the folder themselves. Say that the folder is kept so the user can read `results.json`, for example "left in place after `--run`".

"what does stays in this repo's git directory" is vague, because "what does" has no clear referent. The index files and `results.json` are the only things the script writes there, and the planted commits sit in the object database. Name the artifacts instead, for example "the plant-named index files and results.json stay in a `review-eval-*` folder of this repo's git directory". Line 314-315's comment already gives the WHY.

The reviewer subprocess gets the whole environment (`env: { ...process.env, ... }`). `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB` strips only credential-shaped variables, so path variables set by the user's shell or pnpm (such as PWD/OLDPWD or INIT_CWD, depending on the pnpm version) can still give the main repo's path to the reviewer's shell. The main repo's working tree already names every plant in plain text in tools/review/eval/cases.json, so this change neither opens nor closes that path. The new 'folders around its checkout' wording is still accurate as written.

process_issues.description: The reviewer's Bash call to `git rev-parse` was refused with an approval prompt, so it could not confirm the `--git-common-dir` output or the runner's git version. Its conclusions come from reading the code only.
